perplexity.description:
Sam Brown's debut album Stop!, released in 1988 on A&M Records, is a standout in British pop music of the late 1980s. The album is anchored by its powerful title track, which showcases Brown's dynamic vocal range and emotive delivery. Musically, Stop! blends pop with elements of soul, jazz, and adult contemporary, featuring lush arrangements, strong melodies, and polished production. Brown's songwriting, often co-written with Gregg Sutton and Bruce Brody, demonstrates a maturity and emotional depth that set her apart from many of her contemporaries.

As Sam Brown's first studio album, Stop! established her as a significant new voice in pop music. The album's success was driven by the hit single "Stop!", which became a major chart success in the UK and internationally, helping the album achieve platinum status. Critics praised Brown's vocal prowess and the album's sophisticated sound, noting its blend of pop accessibility and musical craftsmanship. Stop! remains a defining work in Brown's discography, marking the beginning of a career distinguished by her expressive voice and genre-blending style.
